text: SAP write access is not decided for the MVP; current direction is closer to SAP read-only usage, creating delivery and scope risk if SAP write capability is assumed prematurely.
Push notifications are undecided, explicitly not part of the MVP, and only later possible; this creates scope risk if they are treated as an MVP commitment.
The expected user volume ranges from about 200 to 20,000 users, so scalability and performance must be considered without assuming a fixed load profile.
Analytics and KPIs are desired, but measurement concept, technical implementation, tracking, and privacy justification remain open, creating risk of delay or rework.

Offers with discounts above 15% require an approval process, and workflow states are needed: draft, pending approval, approved, sent, accepted, rejected; incomplete workflow support would create business process risk.
EU-only hosting and GDPR-compliant hosting are not the same, so data residency must be clarified to avoid compliance risk.
The handling of SAP price and discount changes, including caching and fallback behavior, remains open and creates integration and correctness risk.
Caching or fallback for SAP data can conflict with data freshness, retention, and privacy constraints, and cache invalidation is complex.
MVP authentication is defined as email/password with mandatory double opt-in; this is a decided, low-risk constraint relative to the open items.
If there is no ticketing system in the MVP, support may rely on unstructured email processing, which creates support and data protection risk.
